note: MPP maps x402 headers onto Payment authentication and x402 exact onto charge; upto and batch-settlement are comparable to sessions. mppx's EVM charge has offered both protocols on one route since 0.6.29 (2026-06-02), 0.9.0 added dual MPP and x402 framework wrappers, and the mppx client prefers the Payment challenge.
Both are HTTP 402 payment protocols; MPP's comparison page, written by its authors, recommends MPP by default. Stripe co-authors MPP and sits on the x402 TSC.
No protocol cross-reference; the shared component is Stripe Shared Payment Tokens, which the stripe method carries and Stripe also uses for agentic checkout.
The Visa-authored card method lets a client add TAP signature headers (in the spec since 2026-03-18); Visa says the card spec and SDK are built on VIC and TAP; mppx adds TAP request attestation.

Tempo's statement only: in Mastercard's 2026-06-10 AP4M release Tempo says it is excited to work with Mastercard on MPP compatibility. Mastercard makes no MPP claim and has no MPP method spec, and its 2026-10-20 brief opening AP4M Early Access says AP4M builds on x402 and names no MPP, Tempo or Stripe.

Complementary in principle (AP2 carries user authorization evidence, MPP settles payment) but no specification binds them and neither repository mentions the other. In AP2, MPP means Merchant Payment Processor.
